AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: WRONG TURN-END SLOT. C#'s player-side AfterSideTurnEnd is audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json step 64 -- it runs AFTER the hand flush -- and the sim HAS that slot: hooks.after_player_turn_end (hooks.py:303-310), whose own docstring says it is Hook.AfterTurnEnd and is 'Distinct from on_player_turn_end, which is Hook.BeforeTurnEnd' (step 48). kusarigama.py:32-33 uses on_player_turn_end, so the reset happens ~16 steps too early. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b08.py b08-kusarigama): the ported StampedePower auto-plays N Attacks from `on_player_turn_end` (powers.py:1023-1039) -- the SAME sim hook -- and its C# home is StampedePower.cs:18 AfterAutoPostPlayPhaseEntered, which turn_structure step 47 places BEFORE step 64. So C# always resets after those Attacks and the sim may not: with Stampede(2) on the player and the executed listener order ['Kusarigama', 'StampedePower'], end_turn leaves _attacks_this_turn=2 where C# leaves 0, and those 2 carry into the next turn -- shifting every 'every 3rd Attack' trigger for the rest of the combat. Both sides ported: Stampede is the Ironclad card cards/stampede.py:36. Bounded, not run-wide: the on_combat_start reset above stops it leaking past the combat. The `participants.Contains(base.Owner.Creature)` filter is structurally satisfied (the sim fires this hook for the player side only). Fix: move the reset to after_player_turn_end, the slot relics/parrying_shield.py:24 already uses. Rule 7: hooks.py, powers.py, cards/stampede.py, relics/parrying_shield.py, src/Core/Models/Powers/StampedePower.cs and audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): AfterCardPlayed fires once per Replay iteration in C# but once per play in the sim, so a replayed Attack advances Kusarigama's counter by 1 instead of 2
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CardModel.cs:1904-1963 builds a fresh CardPlay inside `for (int i = 0; i < playCount; i++)` and fires Hook.AfterCardPlayed at line 1961 INSIDE that loop, so a REPLAYED card advances this relic's per-turn counter once per iteration. The sim's _resolve_card_play runs the whole play-count loop (combat.py:477-494) and calls hooks.on_card_played once, after it (combat.py:514), so a doubled card advances the counter by ONE. This is audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json gap G4 -- one verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3, and that record already labels it LIVE -- observed at this relic's own site; the seam owns the machinery, this record owns the observable. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b08.py b08-replay): with Throwing Axe held, two Strike plays leave _attacks_this_turn=2 and no 6-damage hit, where C# counts 3 and fires the damage. Throwing Axe makes the first card of each combat play twice (relics/throwing_axe.py:30-36) and is granted by the ported Tanx shrine (events/tanx.py); the Spiral and Glam enchantments (enchantments.py:167, 232), One-Two Punch (powers.py:966) and Duplication (powers.py:3919) reach the same combat.py:469 play-count hook. Rule 7: CardModel.cs, combat.py, relics/throwing_axe.py, events/tanx.py, enchantments.py and powers.py are not hashed by this record. The observable is not a rounding detail: because the trigger is `count % 3 == 0`, a DIFFERENT card fires the relic, and every subsequent trigger in the turn is shifted by one play.

C# picks the random target from `Enemies.Where(e => e.IsHittable)` (CombatState.cs:142), and IsHittable is `!IsDead && Hook.ShouldAllowHitting(CombatState, this)` (Creature.cs:285-299). Relic.living_enemies() (relics/base.py:294-297) filters on `not e.is_gone` only. This is the SAME divergence audit/records/relic/bag_of_marbles.json guard G2 records at its own call site, and it carries the same verdict per binding rule 3 -- but it bites harder here, because the set is not just the damage target list, it is the population of an RNG DRAW: `combat_rng.targets.choice(living)` is Rng.NextItem, whose index is scaled by len(seq) (rng.py:248-252), so an unhittable-but-alive enemy changes WHICH enemy is picked even when the pick itself would have been legal, and can also waste the trigger on a target DamageCmd.deal then no-ops on (`should_allow_hitting` returns 0 -- cmds.py:50-51). DORMANT for the same reason bag_of_marbles G2 is: the only ported should_allow_hitting implementers gate on a mid-revival state (IllusionPower powers.py:1572-1575, AdaptablePower powers.py:3372-3375), which cannot coexist with the enemy being alive and un-gone here. Porting any effect that makes a LIVING enemy untargetable makes it live, and in an RNG-visible way (the CombatTargets stream position stays equal but the chosen index diverges). Rule 7: src/Core/Combat/CombatState.cs, src/Core/Entities/Creatures/Creature.cs, relics/base.py, rng.py, cmds.py and powers.py are not hashed by this record.
